newsitem.title: USA: Cash crudes in U.S. slip on U.N. sealing Iraq plan.
newsitem.headline: Cash crudes in U.S. slip on U.N. sealing Iraq plan.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices slipped Monday morning after the United Nations said it finalized an aid distribution plan with Iraq.
Outright cash benchmark August West Texas Intermediate/Cushing stood around 35 cents lower at $18.95-19.05 a barrel, with the Aug/Sep roll at -17 cts.

Cash dealers said grade barrel business took to the sidelines as NYMEX futures selling assumed center stage. Deals were struck for Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at 21 cents over the August benchmark, steady to slightly firmer.
Sweet barrels have found strength from Brent-WTI spreads, and held steady despite Brent fixtures to the U.S. Gulf.

The latest twist on the Iraqi front moves renewed oil exports closer to reality. U.N. negotiators in Baghdad said Monday that discussions on the aid plan were concluded successfully. The plan was expected to be submitted for the approval of U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan next week.
Before Iraq sells oil under the second round of the "oil-for-food" accord, an approved aid plan is necessary, along with a fresh pricing formula.
Despite the Iraq developments, West Texas Sour/Midland differentials held around a $1.30 discount to the marker. WTI/Cushing Postings Plus slipped to $1.81-85 on the widening Aug/Sep roll.
